target_customer: Hospitals and health systems needing per diem clinical staff, and nurses and allied professionals seeking flexible shifts
problem: Hospitals filled gaps through costly staffing agencies while clinicians had little control over where and when they worked. CareRev built a marketplace connecting facilities directly with local vetted professionals.
business_model: Two sided healthcare labor marketplace, margin on shifts worked

founders.name: William Patterson
founders.background_notes: The Series A press release says he worked as a trauma nurse before founding CareRev in 2015.

founders.name: Sofia Pessanha
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; no background found.

technical_complexity.rationale: Mobile marketplace with credential verification and scheduling, standard engineering with operational complexity in vetting and compliance.

defensibility.rationale: Liquidity on both sides and hospital integrations help, but local staffing marketplaces were replicable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large agencies did not stop it. A smaller competitor, IntelyCare, acquired it in early 2026.

market_need_then: Hospital labor was a large cost and agencies took a large margin. The 2021 release cited a source saying labor exceeded half of hospital expenses before COVID, a later source than the founding date.

identity.voice_and_tone: Nurse founded, supportive: created by nurses to bring balance back to care

branding.community_and_virality: No evidence found of merch or fan community.

brand_strength.rationale: Company messaging leans on its nurse founder story, and the brand is known among hospital staffing buyers, but there is no evidence of broader brand pull.

outcome_analysis: CareRev raised a 50 million dollar Series A in April 2021 after claiming fast growth, reached more than 600 facilities by the time of its sale, and was acquired by IntelyCare, announced January 8, 2026. The price is undisclosed and the staffing market is competitive, so the exit looks like consolidation. Founder market fit from a nurse founder helped with trust.
notes: Aggregator listings of a 2016 seed and a 2025 round (5.25M or an unlabelled Series B) are unverified and not recorded. One source said the deal closed December 23, 2025; others give no date. A company blog snippet names Derrek Long as a later CTO and co-founder, but the YC page does not list him, so he is not recorded. The YC page uses a Care Revolutions handle, which hints at the name origin but is unconfirmed. No dated 2016 competitor source was found.
